criteria.text: Diagnosis of hypoparathyroidism (approval criterion 3; closed FDA indication).
Patient is 18 years of age or older (approval criterion 1; FDA adult indication).
Prescribed by or in consultation with an endocrinologist or nephrologist (approval criterion 2).
Baseline albumin-corrected serum calcium ≥7.8 mg/dL utilizing calcium and active vitamin D supplementation (approval criterion 4).
Baseline vitamin D above the lower limit of the normal range (approval criterion 5).
Documented trial and inadequate response to appropriately dosed calcium and active vitamin D for at least 12 weeks after vitamin D restored to normal limits (approval criterion 6).
Will continue calcium and vitamin D supplementation while Yorvipath is titrated to a clinically appropriate dose (approval criterion 7).
Patient does not have acute post-surgical hypoparathyroidism (denial criterion 2).
Patient has not achieved albumin-adjusted serum calcium ≥8.3 mg/dL on calcium and vitamin D supplementation prior to Yorvipath initiation (denial criterion 3).
Patient does not have pseudohypoparathyroidism (denial criterion 4).

notes: Partial encoding from Alaska Medicaid Yorvipath (palopegteriparatide), a PTH(1-34) analog, Criteria Version 1. Original: 2/27/2026; Accepted: 4/17/2026; Effective: 6/1/2026.

Encoded: closed adult hypoparathyroidism indication, approval criteria 1-7 and denial criteria 2-4. Denial criterion 1 mirrors failure to meet approval criteria. Laboratory and therapy documentation require verification.

Limitations of use: not studied for acute post-surgical hypoparathyroidism. Titration scheme evaluated only in adults first achieving albumin-corrected serum calcium of at least 7.8 mg/dL using calcium and active vitamin D.

Cautions (notes only): use only one daily Yorvipath injection. Serious hyper- and hypocalcemia have occurred; monitor serum calcium within 7 to 10 days of initiation and after any dose change, and periodically at maintenance.
Cautions (notes only): not recommended in patients with increased risk of osteosarcoma. Monitor for signs and symptoms of orthostatic hypotension.
Duration (notes only): initial approval up to 6 months; reauthorization up to 12 months.
Quantity limits (notes only): two pens per month; 30 mcg per day. Numeric quantity enforcement is not encoded.
Documentation verification, cautions, monitoring, duration, reauthorization and quantity limits require manual review; this pack remains partial. No alternatives are specified.
